Title: Diagnosis of test `testCompress197`

Details:
The failing test `testCompress197` in `TarArchiveInputStreamTest` attempts to read all entries from a test TAR file `COMPRESS-197.tar` by repeatedly calling `getNextTarEntry()` on a `TarArchiveInputStream`. The loop continues until `getNextTarEntry()` returns null.

The method `getNextTarEntry()` reads the next tar entry by:
- Skipping the remaining bytes of the current entry if any.
- Reading the next tar header record using `getRecord()`.
- Constructing a new `TarArchiveEntry` from the header buffer.
- Handling special GNU long name entries and Pax headers.
- Returning the parsed entry or null if EOF is reached.

The method `getRecord()` reads a tar record by calling `buffer.readRecord()`, which reads a fixed-size record from the underlying input stream. If EOF is detected, it sets an EOF flag and returns null records as indication of end of archive.

The underlying `TarBuffer.readRecord()` reads a record from a block buffer. If all records in the current block have been read, it calls `readBlock()` to read a new block from the input stream using `inStream.read()`.

The `readBlock()` method reads a full block of bytes from the input stream. If EOF occurs before the block is fully read:
- If no bytes were read yet, it returns false indicating EOF.
- If partially read, it fills the remainder of the block buffer with zeros and continues, treating it as a potentially broken but acceptable archive.

The test fails likely due to an issue when reading or skipping entries, possibly encountering an unexpected EOF or malformed entry that triggers an `IOException` or `RuntimeException` inside `getNextTarEntry()` or related reads. For example:
- The `skip()` call in `getNextTarEntry()` could fail to skip unread bytes and throw a RuntimeException.
- An improper header could cause `TarArchiveEntry` construction to throw an `IllegalArgumentException` wrapped as an `IOException`.
- The `read()` method reading entry data could throw an unexpected EOF IOException if the underlying stream ends prematurely.

These errors would be caught in the test and trigger a failure with the associated exception message.

Since the test only reads the entries sequentially and exhausts all entries, the fault most likely lies in the implementation of `getNextTarEntry()`, its use of `buffer.readRecord()`, and handling of partial or broken streams in `readBlock()`.

Suggested methods for fixes:
- `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()`
- `TarArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`
- `TarBuffer.readBlock()`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
